title: Unique section obtained by descent of locally split sums
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be finite etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $F$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Write $B_fW=W\times_XY$ over $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every site object $W$ and every $s\in F(B_fW)$ there is exactly one $u\in F(W)$ such that the following holds. For every site morphism $h:T\to W$ and every finite clopen coproduct $(V_j\xrightarrow{i_j}B_fT)_{j\in J}$ in which each projection to $T$ has inverse $t_j:T\to V_j$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], $F(h)(u)=\sum_j F(i_j\circ t_j)(F(B_fh)(s))$. The finite set may be empty.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Apply the covering theorem to the presieve of all split domains. At each arrow the sums for any two splittings coincide by compatibility applied to identity restrictions. This characterizes a unique value, which can be chosen without choosing arbitrary splitting data. The common-square compatibility theorem proves that these values form a compatible family.

Forget the abelian group structure and apply Mathlib Presieve.IsSheaf.isSheafFor to this covering presieve. The sheaf condition gives a unique amalgamation. Its restriction on any split arrow equals the explicit sum because the local value is characterized independently of the splitting.

Any section satisfying the displayed formulas is an amalgamation of that same compatible family: for each presieve arrow eliminate its existence proof into the equality goal and use the formula for that splitting. Uniqueness of the sheaf amalgamation proves uniqueness in the unchanged statement.
